successCriteria.description: The Notification domain interface is exported and its shape matches the reconciled architecture entity (recipient, type, title, message, related-entity reference, status lifecycle, createdAt, readAt) — verifiable by typecheck against the authoritative entity definition.
The repository interface exposes exactly the five operations create, findByRecipient, markAsSent, markAsRead, and createBatch, plus the create DTO type; all are exported from the module barrel.
create persists a notification row and returns it with status forced to PENDING and readAt forced to null, regardless of any status/readAt values supplied by the caller.
findByRecipient returns the notifications for the given recipient ordered newest-first (created_at DESC), and returns an empty array when the recipient has none.

markAsSent and markAsRead are idempotent — re-marking an already-SENT or already-READ notification succeeds rather than erroring; markAsRead re-stamps readAt to the current timestamp on each call. Both return null when the notification does not exist.

createBatch inserts all provided notifications in a single multi-row statement and returns every persisted row (each forced to PENDING); an empty input array yields an empty result with no database call issued.
The repository constructor accepts an optional transaction client that defaults to the shared pg pool, enabling participation in a caller-owned unit of work per the Transaction Contract.

Jest unit tests in tests/unit/modules/notification/ cover every repository operation against a mocked pool, including the PENDING/null-readAt forcing, idempotent re-marking, not-found null returns, batch empty-input short-circuit, and custom-client injection.
The module barrel re-exports the Notification model, the repository interface, the repository implementation, and the create DTO so downstream modules import only through the barrel.
The module compiles under strict TypeScript (no implicit any, strict null checks) with no use of the any type, and the verification build + jest command exits zero.

constraints: All database access must go through the repository pattern (GP-001 / no-direct-db-outside-repository); the notification repository is the only component that issues SQL against the notifications table.
No use of the any type — use unknown with type guards instead (HARNESS.json no-any rule, severity high).
SQL must use parameterized queries only; no string-interpolated user input (prevents SQL injection and aligns with the existing repository implementations).

Modules import from each other ONLY through their declared public entry point (index.ts); the notification module must not import another module's internals, and downstream consumers must import notification only via its barrel.
No circular dependencies between modules; notification may depend only on shared-types per the reconciled dependency map (notification → shared-types).
No hardcoded secrets, passwords, API keys, or tokens (HARNESS.json no-hardcoded-secrets, severity critical).
No unhandled promise rejections; all async repository errors must be caught and surfaced, not swallowed (GP-006).
Repository methods that must join a caller's transaction accept an optional transaction client defaulting to the shared pool, per the Transaction Contract in the reconciled architecture.
outOfScope: NotificationService and its business logic (fanout orchestration, delivery retry, scheduling) — owned by a later phase per the reconciled module ownership list.
Fastify routes / HTTP controller for notifications — no API surface is part of this phase.
RBAC enforcement and input validation at API boundaries (GP-003/GP-005) — there is no API boundary in this repository-only phase; those apply once routes exist.
Audit record creation for notification writes (GP-002) — notifications are themselves the event record, not a state-changing domain entity requiring its own audit trail in this phase.
Database migrations / schema creation for the notifications table — schema is defined in the reconciled conceptual data model; this phase assumes the table exists.
Integration tests against a real PostgreSQL instance — this phase specifies Jest unit tests with a mocked pool only.
ARCHIVED status transitions and any notification archival/expiry workflow — only PENDING→SENT and →READ transitions are exercised by this phase's repository operations.

ambiguities.description: The reconciled Transaction Contract names PoolClient as the transaction parameter type, but every existing repository (audit, balance, request, policy, notification) implements the optional client as Pick<Pool,'query'> (Queryable) rather than pg.PoolClient. The contract text and the implemented convention diverge in type name while being structurally compatible.
options: Keep the established Queryable = Pick<Pool,'query'> convention for consistency with sibling repositories
Switch to accepting pg.PoolClient explicitly to match the contract text verbatim

ambiguities.description: markAsSent and markAsRead issue unconditional UPDATE ... WHERE id = $1 statements. Whether an already-ARCHIVED notification should be protected from being re-marked SENT/READ is unspecified — the current implementation would overwrite an ARCHIVED status.
options: Allow re-marking from any status (current behaviour — fully idempotent, no guard)
Guard markAsSent/markAsRead to no-op when the row is already ARCHIVED

ambiguities.description: createBatch issues a single multi-row INSERT with no explicit upper bound on input size; a very large fanout batch could exceed PostgreSQL's parameter limit (65535 placeholders ≈ ~10k rows at 6 params each). No batching/chunking strategy is specified.
options: Leave unbounded — rely on callers to keep batches reasonable (matches existing sibling implementations)
Chunk large batches to stay under the parameter limit

entityInvariants.invariant: A newly created Notification always begins its lifecycle in the PENDING status with a null readAt, irrespective of caller-supplied values — PENDING is the only valid initial status.

The status lifecycle is monotonic forward through PENDING → SENT → READ (with ARCHIVED as a later terminal state); markAsSent and markAsRead never throw on re-application of an already-achieved state, preserving idempotency.
readAt is null until the notification is first marked READ; once READ it always carries a non-null timestamp, and each subsequent markAsRead re-stamps readAt to the current time.
A Notification is always associated with exactly one related entity of type 'LeaveRequest' (relatedEntityType is fixed) and one recipient — it cannot exist without both references.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Rejects (propagates) on database failure; never returns a notification with a status other than PENDING or a non-null readAt.
Returns an empty array (not null) when the recipient has no notifications; propagates database errors.
Returns null when no row matches the id; otherwise returns the updated notification. Re-marking an already-SENT row succeeds without error.
Returns null when no row matches the id; otherwise returns the updated notification with a fresh readAt timestamp. Re-marking an already-READ row succeeds without error.

An empty input array short-circuits to an empty result with no database call; a non-empty array issues a single multi-row insert and returns all persisted rows (each PENDING). Propagates database errors.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: No auth at repository layer; RBAC is enforced at the API boundary in a later phase (GP-005).
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Accepts an optional transaction client; defaults to the shared pg pool when omitted.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The Notification entity shape must match the authoritative definition in the reconciled architecture (recipientId, type union of the four leave-transition events, title, message, relatedEntityType fixed to 'LeaveRequest', relatedEntityId, status union PENDING|SENT|READ|ARCHIVED, createdAt, readAt: Date|null) — do not diverge from or extend this contract.
The repository must obtain its default database connection from the shared pg pool exported here, reusing the existing connection rather than constructing a new Pool.

The repository must follow the established Queryable transaction-client pattern used by the sibling repositories (constructor accepts an optional client typed as Pick<Pool,'query'> defaulting to the shared pool), so it can participate in the same caller-owned unit of work as the audit, balance, and request repositories.

The notifications table column contract (id, recipient_id, type, title, message, related_entity_type, related_entity_id, status, created_at, read_at) and the repository behaviour notes (create forces PENDING/null read_at; markAsSent/markAsRead idempotent with read_at re-stamp; createBatch single multi-row INSERT; findByRecipient ordered created_at DESC) documented in the Implementation Notes must be honoured by the implementation.

The module barrel must remain the sole public entry point and must re-export the Notification model, INotificationRepository, NotificationRepository, and CreateNotificationDto, matching the barrel convention used by the audit module.

integrationPoints.why: Per the reconciled dependency map, notification → shared-types; the module may consume shared enum/type definitions if needed, importing only through the shared-types barrel.
The repository defaults to the shared pg Pool for all non-transactional queries; this is the only direct database integration for the module.

Downstream consumer: the leave-request service injects INotificationRepository to fan out LEAVE_SUBMITTED/APPROVED/REJECTED/CANCELLED notifications on lifecycle transitions; this phase establishes the contract that consumer will depend on.
The repository's optional constructor client lets it join a service-owned BEGIN/COMMIT unit of work alongside the leave-request, leave-balance, and audit repositories during the atomic approval flow.
